rulings.challenge_claim: The Prov.15.2 antithesis argued in the row is substantively correct but is built entirely on transliteration, never a quoted Hebrew run (OL brief item 1: a Hebrew claim with no quoted form is insufficient engagement).
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently: consonantal_index.json skeleton check confirms Prov.15.2 shares zero tokens with Prov.15.1 and Prov.15.3, so the row's boundary claim itself is byte-correct. But observed_substrate_signals states the antithesis only via transliterated forms (lashon chakhamim/pi kesilim; teitiv/yabbia) with no Hebrew-script quote of oshb:Prov.15.2 anywhere in the row, violating the TOOLKIT standing rule (quote the original language for every boundary-relevant original-language claim) and the OL brief's own item 1. Evidentiary-hygiene gap, not a boundary error.
rulings.remedy: Splice a byte-tier Hebrew quote of the antithesis pair from verse_map_oshb.json into observed_substrate_signals/device_notes, re-collated via collate.py to byte tier before resubmission. Cure test: collate.py --ref oshb:Prov.15.2 --quote <spliced text> returns tier=byte.

rulings.challenge_claim: The antithesis and Prov.15.32 cross-reference for Prov.15.5 are correct, but the row's transliteration 'evil' for the verse's actual subject is a homograph collision with the English word for wickedness that a quoted Hebrew run would have prevented.
rulings.grounds: Independently confirmed from bytes: oshb:Prov.15.5 opens אֱוִ֗יל ("fool"), and web:Prov.15.5 renders "A fool despises his father's correction...". The row's own rationale field correctly says "fool," but observed_substrate_signals contains the inconsistent gloss "evil" ("subject pair evil / shomer tokhachat"), which risks the moral-wickedness sense rather than the actual subject. This compounds the same missing-Hebrew-quote hygiene gap as P07-002/003/007 -- OL's own diagnosis (a quoted Hebrew run would have prevented the collision) is correct. The eleven-verse gap to Prov.15.32 and the ch.15 catchword-adjacency figure (7/32, prov_device_inventory.json) both independently check out, so the single_proverb boundary call itself is unaffected.
rulings.remedy: Correct "evil" to "fool" in observed_substrate_signals; quote אֱוִ֗יל (spliced from oshb bytes) inline, byte-collated. Cure test: re-collate the corrected quote+gloss at byte tier and confirm the gloss reads "fool", not "evil".

rulings.challenge_claim: LF: the rationale's colon-position description of the shared 'abomination to YHWH' construct phrase is byte-false -- it does not 'open the second colon' in either verse. OL independently raised the identical accent-based finding within its own P07-008 item.
rulings.grounds: Independently re-derived a third time from oshb bytes plus Unicode codepoint check (U+0591 ETNAHTA): in oshb:Prov.15.8 (זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה וּתְפִלַּ֖ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים רְצוֹנֽוֹ), ETNAHTA falls on the word for YHWH (word 4 of 7) -- the shared phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה is the CLOSE of the pre-atnach first colon (זֶ֣בַח רְ֭שָׁעִים תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה), not the opening of a second colon (colon 2 = וּתְפִלַּ֖ת יְשָׁרִ֣ים רְצוֹנֽוֹ, which does not contain the phrase at all). In oshb:Prov.15.9 (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע וּמְרַדֵּ֖ף צְדָקָ֣ה יֶאֱהָֽב), ETNAHTA falls on the word for 'wicked' (word 4 of 7) -- the phrase תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה OPENS the pre-atnach first colon / the verse itself (תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה דֶּ֣רֶךְ רָשָׁ֑ע), again not a second colon. The row's 'both open their second colon' claim is therefore byte-false at the accent tier. LF and OL reached this identical conclusion independently via the identical accent-based method -- this is the SAME defect in both packets, not two distinct findings. It is a structural-description defect in the stated warrant; independently re-confirmed it does not by itself unseat the underlying sweep digit (sweep.py --skel returns 11 verses book-wide: Prov.3.32, Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.15.9, Prov.15.26, Prov.16.5, Prov.17.15, Prov.20.10, Prov.20.23, and Prov.15.8-Prov.15.9 is the ONLY adjacent pair among them).
rulings.remedy: Rewrite the rationale's structural claim to state the accent-verified positions accurately: תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְהוָ֑ה is colon-1-final in 15:8; תּוֹעֲבַ֣ת יְ֭הוָה is colon-1/verse-initial in 15:9 -- a hook-word straddling the verse boundary, not a uniform 'opens the second colon' pattern. Cure test: re-derive the U+0591 ETNAHTA codepoint position in both spliced oshb strings and confirm the corrected wording matches; re-collate both quoted Hebrew runs to byte tier via collate.py.

rulings.challenge_claim: The proverb_cluster call for Prov.15.8-15.9 rests on a construct phrase that is an 11-verse book-wide macro-genre formula rather than a two-verse-only local catchword; recommend re-arguing as two single_proverb rows, or naming the formula-class explicitly and grounding cohesion in a genuinely local feature instead.
rulings.grounds: Re-derived independently from bytes on both sides of this disagreement. (1) sweep.py --skel confirms the phrase sweeps to 11 verses book-wide (Prov.3.32, Prov.11.1, Prov.11.20, Prov.12.22, Prov.15.8, Prov.15.9, Prov.15.26, Prov.16.5, Prov.17.15, Prov.20.10, Prov.20.23), of which Prov.15.8-Prov.15.9 is the ONLY adjacent consecutive pair -- no other pair among the 11 sites is adjacent. This uniqueness is itself byte-grounded evidence and is structurally comparable to the owner's own worked example of valid C2 cluster evidence, the 26:4-5 answer/answer-not pair (LF's reading). (2) Independently checked the closing word of each occurrence: oshb:Prov.11.1, oshb:Prov.12.22, and oshb:Prov.15.8 all close their construct-phrase clause on the same word (רְצוֹנֽוֹ, 'his delight'), confirming OL's point that the phrase belongs to a recurring antithetic sub-template independently deployed by the redactor at 3+ non-adjacent sites in the book, not a bespoke two-verse coinage (OL's reading). Both facts are simultaneously true. The owner's Section 6 text lists 'catchword chains' and 'pair grouping' as valid cluster evidence in the same breath as warning that a cluster whose only glue is a shared THEME is over-clustering -- and this case (an exact repeated 2-word construct phrase, book-wide-attested, uniquely adjacent at one site) does not map cleanly onto either the 26:4-5 hapax-pairing paradigm or the vague-shared-theme paradigm the rule was written against. This is a genuine owner-level contested reading of where the C2 cluster-evidence bar sits, not a defect resolvable by further byte-checking -- both primaries' underlying byte claims are independently confirmed correct and mutually compatible; they diverge only on the policy weight to give them. Escalating per the launch brief's explicit guidance for exactly this class of disagreement.
